newsitem.title: UK: Crude palm oil prices in Europe hit by export data.
newsitem.headline: Crude palm oil prices in Europe hit by export data.

text.p: Crude palm oil prices in Europe on Thursday came under further pressure following the release of lower-than-expected Malaysian export estimates.
Malaysian cargo surveyor Societe Generale de Surveillance (SGS) Malaysia Sdn Bhd put local palm oil exports for January 1-15 at 255,320 tonnes against 406,924 in December 1-15.
"Sentiment has turned against palm oil and some people are now wondering if the recent rise in prices was justified," said a trader.

Traders said sentiment was also being affacted by scepticism over the Malaysian stock figures issued on Wednesday by PORLA which showed a high local disappearence of around 163,000 tonnes and lower than expected exports.
Crude palm oil cif Europe was offered around $5 down after Mar traded at 550 and Apr/Jun at $555 and $550 a tonne cif.
Products were mixed with RBD palm oil $2.50 up and olein $2.50 down after Feb RBD traded at $565 a tonne.
Feb olein fetched $590 and $592.50, Mar $582.50 and $575 and Apr/Jun $573.50 a tonne fob Malaysia ports.
Lauric oils were quiet and mostly lower with sellers unchanged to $2.50 down.
Soft oils were lower following the easier Chicago soyoil futures close on Wednesday, but sellers were reluctant to mark prices down too far owing to the firm end to the soybean session.
Dutch soy oil sellers were 0.25 to 0.50 guilders down while rape oil was 0.50 guilders lower in tradeless markets.
The premium for rape oil over soyoil, based on sellers' prices, was one guilder to par at midday against 1.50 to par at Wednesday's close. --Jim Ballantyne, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8062
